title: Vandy – IP Glucose Tolerance Test
author: Louise Lantier
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yzzfx76

steps.title: Prepare Mice and Materials
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice and necessary equipment for the glucose tolerance test.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the mice (note: for mice of differing fat mass, dosing the bolus of glucose on lean mass is recommended, requiring body composition).
Fast mice for 5 hours by transferring them to individual cages or containers.
Prepare an experiment record sheet, glucose measurement sticks, and syringes for IP injection of Dextrose solution.

steps.title: Calculate Glucose Dosage
steps.instruction: Determine the required volume of 20% Dextrose solution for each mouse to achieve a dose of 2g dextrose/kg body mass.

substeps.instruction: Calculate volume using the formula: 20% Dextrose (μl) = 10 x body weight (g).
Record the calculated volume for each individual mouse on the record sheet.

steps.title: Collect Baseline Glucose and Blood
steps.instruction: Obtain baseline glucose levels and initial blood samples for insulin measurement.

substeps.instruction: Cut the tip of the tail using clean surgical scissors.
Place a small drop of blood (<5μl) on a blood glucose meter test strip to record baseline glucose (t = 0).
Collect 40µL of whole blood in a tube (e.g., Sarstedt’s Microvette® CB 300 cat # 16.443.100 for Heparin or cat # 16.444.100 for EDTA).
Spin blood for 1min at 13k rpm and collect 25µL of plasma in a new tube.
Collect an additional 20µL of plasma in a clean tube and store on ice.

steps.title: Administer Glucose Injection
steps.instruction: Inject the mouse intraperitoneally (IP) with the pre-calculated volume of 20% Dextrose solution and start the timer.

steps.title: Monitor Glucose and Collect Plasma
steps.instruction: Measure blood glucose and collect plasma samples at specified time intervals post-injection.

substeps.instruction: Measure blood glucose levels at 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90, and 120 minutes.
Collect 20µl plasma samples for insulin determination at 10, 30, 60, and 120 minutes.
For each sample, remove the clot from the first incision to restart bleeding; massage the tail if blood flow is inadequate.
Place a small drop of blood on a new test strip and record results on the record sheet.
Briefly apply pressure to the incision after each measurement to minimize further blood loss.

steps.title: Post-Experiment Processing
steps.instruction: Finalize the experiment and store samples.

substeps.instruction: Euthanize mice for tissue collection or place them in a clean cage with water and food available ad libitum for recovery.
Monitor mice carefully for any abnormal behavior.
Store plasma samples in a -20 or -80ºC freezer until analysis.
